failures.evidence: With any NATS already answering on E2E_NATS_PORT (a server left by an earlier run, or a second run at the same time), the script's own natsd exits at once with '[FTL] Error listening on port: 127.0.0.1:14222, "listen tcp 127.0.0.1:14222: bind: address already in use"', wait_for_nats (scripts/e2e-local.sh, the curl INFO loop) reads the other server's INFO greeting, and the script runs the whole acceptance against that server, prints 'PASS: topic set, structured payloads, checks settlement, and both renderers match the local acceptance contract' and exits 0, leaving ENVOY_NOTIFICATIONS and the four KV buckets in that server's store. Reproduced in this pod at e8af3445dd29 by starting out/e2e/natsd -p 14222 -js -store_dir <dir> and then bash scripts/e2e-local.sh. On main, docker run -p 14222:4222 would refuse a held port [inference from Docker's port publishing; main cannot run in a pod]. Red test: packages/envoy/scripts/e2e-local.test.sh, case 'refuses to run against a NATS server it did not start' (commit 9b4fa7896d56): a bun stand-in greets 'INFO {...}' on a free port, the driver runs with E2E_NATS_PORT set to it, and the test requires a non-zero exit whose output carries 'address already in use'. Command: cd packages/envoy && bash scripts/e2e-local.test.sh -> 'FAIL: the driver did not report that its own NATS server could not bind port <n>' after 'ERR: listener did not become healthy within 30 seconds.', exit 1. A fix that makes wait_for_nats fail when kill -0 "$nats_pid" fails (printing nats.log) and accept the greeting only once nats.log holds 'Server is ready' turned it green in a throwaway copy, and the full e2e-local.sh still passed there; a kill -0 check alone did not (natsd is still alive when the first greeting arrives). No CI step runs scripts/e2e-local.test.sh (grep of .github/ finds only e2e-local.sh in envoy-e2e-local), so the case locks nothing until a step runs it; envoy-e2e-local, which has go and bun, is the natural place.
